newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 23.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company -- CBI IS POISED TO BACK EUROPEAN SINGLE CURRENCY

The Confederation of British Industry is prepared to go against the trend of Euroscepticism, which was highlighted by the announcement that millionaire Paul Sykes would launch a newspaper campaign urging EMU opponents to vote Conservative. The CBI has released a document giving three options: sterling should join EMU in the long term, sterling should join in 1999 or sterling should join shortly after having observed how well the new currency performs. The CBI document was an embarrassment to its president, Colin Marshall, who is a Tory sympathiser.
-- HALIFAX WINDFALLS COULD RISE TO AVERAGE OF 1700 STG

Halifax building society of the UK has said its membership has been cut to 7.6 million people, which could result in a surge of payouts to members averaging 1,700 stg. Halifax will undergo a 13 billion stg floatation in June that will provide shareholders 200 shares each. It is possible Halifax could have the same success as Alliance & Leicester, which floated on Monday at share prices well above predicted levels.
-- GERMAN DEFICIT 'NO BAR' TO EMU START

Six of Germany's leading economic research institutes have forecast that the 1997 budget deficit of the country would be above the 3 percent of GDP prescribed for EMU. The institutes were quick to add that they did not believe the predictions would affect Germany's entry into the single currency, as the decision was not based solely on economic status. The institute has predicted the deficit would fall below 2.8 percent in 1998.
-- NOMURA HANDS BACK CO-OP DOCUMENTS AFTER COURT ORDER

Documents that the Nomura International Bank had provided to Andrew Regan's bank, Hambros, have been returned to the Co-operative wholesale Society, the business Regan is planning a hostile takeover on. A high court ruling had ordered the return of the confidential papers from Regan and other parties. Meanwhile, the Serious Fraud Office has announced it would terminate plans to investigate the 2.4-million-sterling payment made in 1995 by food company Hobson, then owned by Rehan.
-- GUNBOAT DIPLOMACY TO PUT THE WIND IN UK SALES

Beginning this December in Barcelona aboard the UK aircraft carrier Invincible, the Royal Navy, in conjunction with British Invisibles, will begin a series of events intended to help encourage UK services exports. Aboard the carrier, business representatives will fund and host cocktail parties for foreign investors and similar representatives in the foreign ports. The scheme is intended to improve promotion of British financial services, which make up a large portion of UK exports but take a back seat to merchandise in government promotional efforts.
-- BUSINESS 'MUST IMPROVE ITS IMAGE'

The director general of the UK Institute of Directors, Tim Melville-Ross, is set to announce plans to improve the country's business image at the IoD's annual convention on Wednesday. Melville-Ross will propose using business-linked materials in schools, encourage business leaders to discuss business values and promote television programming related to business issues. His chief claim is that without improved public understanding of the area, the business climate will deteriorate.
-- SMITHKLINE BEECHAM PROFITS UP 8 PERCENT

The UK's second biggest drugs company, SmithKline Beecham, reported its first quarter pre-tax profit grew eight percent to 418 million stg. Chief executive Jan Leschly said the strength of the sterling was having a "dramatic effect" on its published figures and the increase would have been 19 percent had the currency remained constant. A severe influenza season in North America boosted sales of SB's Augmentin, with sales rising 29 percent, while sales in consumer health care rose 18 percent.
-- P&O HOPES FOR EARLY MERGER DECISION

UK shipping and property company P&O hopes to hear before the end of the May if it will be allowed to merge its cross-channel ferry operations with Stena Line, despite Stena's comments that late approval could result in missing the summer season. P&O has said Stena need not worry as both parties were aiming for a common goal. If the merger goes as planned, P&O could save 75 million stg annually on costs of 280 million stg.
-- REED EXECUTIVE TO DELIST SOME SHARES TO AVOID TAX

Alec Reed, founder of recruitment company Reed Executive, has said he will delist some of his shares in the firm to ensure it remains in his family's control by avoiding inheritance tax. Reed believes the decision to go public in 1971 was a mistake and has cost it value over the years. The decision should not affect shareholders or any of Reed's 900 private investors.
-- CULLENS RECEIVES OFFER

London-based convenience store chain Cullens has said it has received a bid approach, but has refused to identify the bidder. It is believed the bidder was a private convenience store group and has made a cash bid for the chain. Cullen, which manages shops in Mobile petrol station forecourts, is expected to retain its name should a deal go through.
